name: Kepler-11
class_label_origin: Published planet/system identification; size categories require stellar information beyond the light curve. No physical size or habitability is inferred here.
observable_signature: Six distinct recurring transit sequences with different periods, depths and durations

photometry.processing: All listed long-cadence FITS; SAP_QUALITY == 0, finite positive PDC flux and error. Split at gaps >0.3 d; skip pieces <10 points or <5 unmasked points. Mask all catalog transit centers ±0.8 duration; interpolate masked values only for estimating a 1-day odd-window running-median trend (nearest edges); divide observed flux and error by that trend. No synthetic observations or outlier clipping. Quarter column preserved.

methods.central_depth: Per cycle: mean flux at duration < abs(time from transit) < 2 duration minus mean central flux at abs(time from transit) < 0.3 duration; convert to ppm. Average usable cycle depths equally. Other planet transits masked ±0.8 duration; require >=2 central and >=6 baseline points per cycle. This is a central-window contrast, not a fitted maximum depth.
methods.uncertainty: Standard deviation of 1000 bootstrap resamples of usable transit cycles; seed 20260906; includes event-to-event scatter, excludes ephemeris, detrending and blending uncertainties.
methods.odd_even: Separate averages of usable cycles by parity around catalog epoch; descriptive only, not an EB rejection test.
methods.folded_image: Gray retained points and 40 equal time-bin means with standard-error bars; full-baseline fold centered on catalog linear ephemeris; no individual transit-time corrections.
methods.catalog: Composite catalog quantities can originate in different publications; reference ephemerides are not a new joint fit. TTVs and ephemeris uncertainty may broaden the display.
methods.sample_counts: central_sample_count and baseline_sample_count count all points passing their masks, including cycles subsequently excluded from the depth average. used_cycle_central_sample_count and used_cycle_baseline_sample_count count only points in the usable per_transit records.

source.credit: NASA Kepler / MAST and NASA Exoplanet Archive

classification_limit: A shallow dip is not by itself an Earth-sized planet. Absolute size requires a host-star radius and a transit model; source localization and false-positive vetting are separate. These are published reference systems, not new discoveries.
